claude_only.name: Which identifier is authoritative for this form definition: the issuing authority's official form number, a governed canonical URI, or a locally minted UUID?
How is a substantive new version distinguished from an editorial correction, and which algorithm orders versions?
In which publication state is the instrument, and during exactly which period may it accept new submissions?
Which authority owns the instrument and may approve or retire a version?
Is each item's link identifier unique within the instrument and immutable across the version lineage, and is reuse for a different question forbidden?
How are groups, repeating groups and display-only items distinguished from answerable questions?
Must the response tree mirror the definition tree exactly, including nesting and sibling order?
Is the presentation and transmission order of items semantically significant for interpretation or for legal completeness?
Which datatype system defines the permitted value type for each item, and is it declared in the instrument or inherited from a schema?
Is the answer restricted to a governed value set, and may free text be supplied alongside or instead of a coded option?
For quantity answers, which unit of measure and which precision or significant figures are required?
Which value-domain rules are declared in the instrument versus enforced only by the receiving system, and is any format keyword treated as an assertion rather than an annotation?
Under what conditions is each item enabled, and how are multiple conditions combined?
Are values for disabled or irrelevant items pruned from the transmitted payload, retained as explicit nulls, or retained with a coded reason?
Which items are computed rather than entered, and is the computation re-evaluated authoritatively by the receiver at submission time?
How are dependency cycles among conditional and calculated items detected, and is a cyclic instrument rejected at publication?
Which statutory or delegated authority permits or compels this collection, and is response mandatory, voluntary, or required to obtain a benefit?
What control number and expiration date are displayed, and how are submissions received after expiry handled?
What are the stated principal purposes and routine uses of the collected data, and where are they published?
What per-respondent burden is estimated, how was it derived, and what evidence of practical utility supports the collection?
Which identifier is authoritative for this submission: the receiving authority's receipt or filing number, the submitter's own reference, or an internally minted UUID?
To exactly which instrument version is this submission bound, and is that binding immutable once the submission leaves draft?
What happens to an in-progress draft when the bound instrument version is superseded or retired?
What is this submission about, and which prior request, order or submission is it based on or part of?
How are multiple answers to one item and repeated groups represented so that duplicates are not collapsed and occurrence identity is preserved?
How is not asked distinguished from disabled by logic, left blank, not applicable and declined to answer?
Is the transmitted order of answer entries semantically significant, and must it be preserved through every projection?
Is a partial payload a valid instance, and which items may be absent while the package remains well-formed?
Which attached document is the lead document and which are connected or supporting, and does that role affect adjudication?
What filename, media type, character encoding and size limits apply, and how are unsafe or ambiguous filenames neutralised on receipt?
Is the attachment carried inline in the package or referenced by URI, and which party guarantees its continued availability for the retention period?
What integrity value is recorded so the attachment can later be proven unaltered and reproduced as an accurate and complete copy?
Which constraint is declared on each item and which validity state does its failure produce?
Which items are barred from constraint validation because they are disabled, read-only or irrelevant, and therefore never block submission?
Is a declared format treated as a non-blocking annotation or as an enforced assertion, and who made that choice?
May validation be deliberately bypassed to save an incomplete draft, and under whose authority is the bypass recorded?
When the sending and receiving systems disagree on validity, whose verdict is authoritative and how is the disagreement recorded?
Is the full constraint set re-evaluated on receipt, and against which instrument version - the bound one or the current one?
How is a validation outcome recorded so it can be replayed and audited after rule sets have changed?
What is the disposition of a payload that passes structural validation but fails a business or eligibility rule?
What is the current status of the submission, and is status a modifier that changes how the payload may lawfully be used?
Are review status and recording or docketing status tracked separately, and what does it mean when they disagree?
Is status tracked per item or per document as well as per submission, and does a part-level rejection reject the whole?
Which status values mean the content must not be used for clinical, legal, statistical or operational purposes?
Which status transitions are permitted, which are terminal, and what precondition guards each one?
What operational system check prevents steps from being performed out of order, for example signing before validation completes?
Which role is authorised to trigger each transition, and how is that authority checked at execution time?
May a submission in a terminal state be reopened, and what record must that create?
Who reviewed the submission and under what delegated authority did they accept, reject or return it?
Which coded reason and human-readable explanation accompany a rejection or return, and are they drawn from a governed code list?
Can a submission be partly accepted, and what is the status and disposition of the unaccepted parts?
Does acceptance take effect from the original receipt time or from the decision time, and which governs any deadline?
Is a correction recorded as a new version of the same submission or as a new submission that supersedes the prior one, and who decided that convention?
What explicitly links a resubmission to the rejected or withdrawn submission it replaces?
Is superseded or entered-in-error content retained and retrievable, and how is it excluded from downstream use without being destroyed?
Who may withdraw a submission and up to which point in the lifecycle?
Who supplied the answers, who recorded them and who transmitted the package, and are any of these the same party?
Is the submission made on behalf of another party, and what evidence establishes that representation?
At which site, organisational unit or jurisdiction was the data captured, and does that affect which rules apply?
What identity proofing or authentication was performed on the submitter before the package was accepted?
What exact declaration or certification text did the signer accept, and what meaning is attached to the signature?
By what method was the record signed, and how is the signature bound to this exact payload so it cannot be excised or transferred to another record?
What identity assurance and authority check were performed before the signature was accepted?
Is the signature manifestation reproducible in human-readable form on any export or printed copy?
What audit entry is generated for each create, modify and delete action on the submission, and does it capture the prior value?
For which classes of change is a reason for change mandatory, and is a free-text reason acceptable or must it be coded?
Is the audit trail generated independently of the operator and protected from modification or deletion by the parties it records?
For how long is the audit trail retained relative to the submission itself, and is it disposed of together with the record?
Which distinct time points are recorded for this submission: started, last saved, authored, signed, transmitted, received, decided and disposed?
How is event time (when the respondent answered or signed) kept separate from observation or ingestion time (when the receiver recorded it), and which is used for reporting?
In which timezone is a deadline evaluated, and is an explicit offset recorded with every stored timestamp?
If a submission is rejected and corrected within a grace period, which time counts for deadline compliance?
How long may a draft remain untouched before it expires, and is the respondent warned before expiry?
Which roles may read, amend, decide on or export the submission, and at what granularity is that authorisation expressed?
Which items carry heightened sensitivity requiring separate authorisation or separate storage?
Is any part of the submission sealed or restricted from the submitting or responding parties themselves?
How is each access to and export of a submission logged, and are denied attempts recorded too?
Is any version of this submission published or disclosed beyond the receiving authority, and to whom?
Which items or document regions must be redacted before release, and under which rule set?
Who authorises release, and is the authorisation recorded separately from the release itself?
Is the redacted release a distinct artifact with its own identifier and integrity value, so it is never confused with the original?
Which event starts the retention clock - receipt, final decision, or closure of the parent matter - and how long is the period?
Under which named disposition authority is the submission destroyed or transferred, and to which destination?
How are abandoned drafts and never-submitted answers disposed of differently from accepted submissions?
How is an erasure or correction request from the respondent reconciled with a statutory retention obligation, and is a refusal recorded?
Is a legal hold or preservation order in force that suspends the disposition schedule?
Which serialization is the canonical form for digesting and signing, as distinct from the transport encodings permitted on the wire?
What character encoding is asserted for text values, and how is it signalled when the transport cannot carry an explicit declaration?
How are hierarchical and repeating groups represented in a flat name/value encoding without loss of nesting or occurrence identity?
Which encodings are permitted for a given channel, and who decides when they diverge from the instrument's declared serialization?
To which target data element does each item map, and is the mapping declared in the instrument or maintained externally?
Once answers are extracted downstream, is the extracted record authoritative or does the submission remain the source of truth?
How is the exact question wording preserved when answers are extracted into semantically typed records that discard phrasing?
How are extraction failures surfaced without invalidating an otherwise accepted submission?
Through which channel and endpoint was the submission transmitted, and was acceptance acknowledged synchronously or asynchronously?
What does the acknowledgement contain that lets the submitter prove the package was received at a particular instant?
How are transport errors distinguished from structural rejections and from business rejections in the response?
What subsequent notification is owed to the submitter, and within what interval must it arrive?
Which key determines that two received packages are the same submission rather than two legitimately distinct ones?
Within what window is a repeated transmission treated as a retry rather than a new submission?
What is returned when a duplicate is detected - the original receipt, a conflict error, or a new receipt referencing the original?
For each failed constraint, is the erroneous item identified and the error described in text rather than by colour or position alone?
Is a correction suggestion provided when one is known, and is it deliberately withheld where suggesting it would compromise security or purpose?
Are validation results and progress exposed programmatically so assistive technology is notified without moving focus?
Does every item requiring input carry a label or instruction, and do headings and labels describe topic or purpose?
Is this submission legally binding, financial, or a modification of user-controlled data, and therefore subject to the reversible, checked or confirmed requirement?
Is a review-and-confirm step presented before irreversible submission, and is the respondent's confirmation itself recorded?
Is information the respondent already supplied in the same process re-requested, and if so on what justification?
Is the purpose of each personal-data input programmatically identified so autofill and personalisation can operate?
What measured time to complete is observed, and how does it compare with the published burden estimate?
What proportion of started submissions are abandoned, and at which item does abandonment concentrate?
Which items generate the most validation failures or rejections, and has the instrument been revised in response?
What evidence shows the collected data is actually used, and which items have never been consumed downstream?

grok_only.name: What is the authoritative master-system identifier of this instrument, and which issuing system owns it?
What globally unique canonical IRI or URL identifies this questionnaire or notice definition across servers?
What business version string and version-comparison algorithm apply, and is this version still the current authorized instrument?
What human titles, computer-friendly name and language of authoring apply to this instrument?
Does this instrument display a currently valid OMB control number, and what is that number and its expiration?
Is the respondent informed that they are not required to respond unless a currently valid control number is displayed?
What is the clearance type and status of this collection (standard, generic, emergency, extension, revision, reinstatement)?
If a control number is present, which agency-bureau prefix and collection suffix does it encode?
What unique link identifier within the instrument identifies this group or question, and is uniqueness enforced?
How is this item nested, ordered and typed (group, question, display), and may it repeat?
What prompt, label, help, hint and instructional text are shown, and in which language?
Does this item bind to an external data-element definition or structure so answers can later be extracted?
What datatype, requiredness and cardinality apply to answers for this item?
What pattern, range, step, length limits or answer-option value set constrain the permitted values?
Under what expressions or prior answers is this item relevant or enabled, and is it read-only or disabled?
If the item is a selection, are options static, bound to a value set, or generated from instance data?
What master-system identifier and additional business identifiers uniquely identify this response package?
Which exact instrument canonical and version was this response answered against?
What is the current lifecycle status, who set it, and at what time?
Is this a complete or partial list of answers, and are further changes still expected?
When was this response last modified by the user, with seconds and an explicit offset or Z?
What is the business event time of the answers versus the observation or ingestion time into the receiving system?
During which encounter, session or filing window was this response created, and is it tightly associated with that context?
Who or what is the subject of these answers, and is that party different from the source who answered?
Which individual, organization or device answered the questions about the subject?
Which individual, organization or device received the answers and recorded them in the system?
What request, care plan, procedure or observation does this response fulfill or form part of?
What answer values were recorded for each link-id, including datatype, coding and empty-but-relevant omissions?
For repeating groups, what instance indexes exist and how do nested answers attach to each repeat?
Which file uploads are part of this package, with filename, media type, size and integrity hash?
Were hidden, calculated or directionality fields included in the submitted entry list?
For each relevant item, is it valid, and which suffering states or failed constraints apply?
Is the selected instance or response package valid for submission under the current validate flag?
Have calculate, rebuild and revalidate been run since the last user or action mutation?
Which failures come from schema or datatype versus XForms or questionnaire model-item properties versus custom business rules?
Which constraints were evaluated client-side, which server-side, and were they equivalent?
Is save-incomplete permitted, which submitter control used novalidate, and where is the unfinished package stored?
Was a submit attempted only to test validity without transmitting a resource?
Are required items identified both in visible labels and programmatically (required and aria-required)?
What text descriptions identify missing required fields and values outside required format, and in which language?
Which value domains accept multiple notations rather than a single rigid pattern?
Was the respondent given a review step to inspect and correct answers before the definitive submit?
What confirmation mechanism was required for irreversible or legal, financial or data-destroying actions?
After submit, within what stated duration may the respondent amend or cancel, and has that window closed?
What destination resource, method, headers and mediation (HTTP, SOAP, file, dialog-close) were used for this submit?
How was the payload serialized, which nodes or named controls were included, and was relevance pruning applied?
Did submission succeed or fail, at what event times, and what receipt, status code, response headers or error reason were returned?
Did the submission replace all or part of instance data with the server response, and which target node was replaced?
Has this package been amended after completion, and what prior versions and change descriptions exist?
If this is a published notice, is the update a change notice, and does it stay within permitted non-significant changes?
Was the response stopped without completion or entered in error and voided, and who authorized that terminal state?
If the instrument changed, was the change de minimis, non-substantive, or a revision requiring re-clearance?
What digest or integrity value binds the received payload, and was it verified?
Was the package signed or sealed, at what assurance, by which signer, and is the signature object stored elsewhere?
Has this completed submission been captured as a record, with which record identifier and capture time?
What confidentiality pledge was made to respondents, under what authority, and which security policy supports it?
Who may read this instrument, this response, its uploads and its validation report, and under which compartment or role?
What PII or confidential classes are present, and which legal exceptions (criminal investigation, audit of a named party, intelligence) take the collection outside PRA?
What retention applies to the instrument, to drafts, to submitted responses and to uploads, and when is deletion or destruction authorized?
May the source request erasure or correction, and does a cooling-off or records schedule override that request?
Was this response pre-populated, from which sources, and which answers were then edited by a human?
Into which target records or resources were answers extracted after submit, and with what mapping?
Which external standards is this instance aligned to, and which known conflicts or non-conformances apply?
If this instrument is an eForms notice, what form type and subtype govern mandatory and conditionally mandatory fields?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
